description: Push cart built around a large flat steel griddle plate, with a dough ball tray, squeeze bottles of condensed milk and a gas bottle underneath.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Compact push cart built around a large flat round steel griddle plate set into the counter top, shallow tray of oiled dough balls beside it, upright squeeze bottles and a sugar shaker at the back rail, gas cylinder stowed on the lower shelf, metal spatula resting on the plate rim Materials: Black oil-seasoned griddle plate with burnt sugar rings, glossy oiled dough, greasy stainless counter, scratched squeeze bottles, dented gas cylinder with faded paint.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,724/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases. Open bay: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Ten-band proxy comparison 0.0219 width / 0.0154 depth of H, against 0.212 / 0.017 for the first build, with bands 0-8 all inside 0.028. Envelope 1.11 x 1.394 x 0.72 m; cabinet 0.10-1.06 open at the front, counter at 1.06, bottles to 1.33.
featureReviews.notes: THE WIDTH WAS A DECLARED ASPECT RATIO, and the band table said so in a way a plate never could: the first build was a near-CONSTANT +0.19 of H too wide in every one of bands 0-7 while the depth matched to 0.017. A uniform offset across every band is an aspect, not a shape. The proxy wants 0.78 H = 1.09 m and the plate agrees independently -- its silhouette bbox is w/h 0.896, which a declared 1.30 projects as 1.047 (1.30 cos35 + 0.70 sin35, over 1.40) and 1.08 projects as 0.90. Fixing that left the whole remaining residual in ONE band: band 9 read +0.399 while every other band was inside 0.028, because the top tenth of the model contained the RAIL. The tallest squeeze bottle stopped at 1.334, 66 mm short of the declared height, so the height was set by nothing in particular and the rail top at 1.230 fell inside band 9. The plate shows the bottles standing well clear of the rail; built that way the rail drops into band 8, band 9 holds only the bottles at 0.244 H against the proxy's 0.275, and the built height reaches 1.394.

featureReviews.evidence: r 0.30 dish standing 32 mm proud of the counter with a 22 mm lip and a narrow rust ring at 0.60-0.82 of the radius; 56% of the corrected counter width, where the plate shows just over half.
featureReviews.notes: Two faults, and the second was caused by fixing the first. The pan is held on CHROMA: the plate measures its centre at #47382d, luma 59 and saturation 0.37, and a NEUTRAL grey at luma 59 sits inside the turntable gate's backdrop test (|59-58| <= 24 and sat <= 0.16), so the iron is authored warm and dark rather than lifted off its measurement. The first correction authored it at luma 119 on the SIDE-face transfer and it came back a tan doughnut -- a round, near-horizontal top face renders well ABOVE that transfer, which only holds for the vertical panels it was probed on. And the scorch ring at 0.34-0.78 of the radius was not a ring at all: it covered the pan and the griddle rendered as one flat tan plate.

featureReviews.evidence: Red gas bottle in the bay, four bottles and a shaker at the rail, tray with eight dough balls, spatula.

notes: The large flat round griddle plate set into the counter is the whole identity of this prop -- without it the cart reads as any generic vendor trolley, so the plate must stay wide, flat and visually dominant rather than being reduced to a hotplate detail. Kept on the derived medium budget rather than overridden upward: the cart body and the griddle are both steel and can share one material with roughness and colour carried by the texture, and there is no transparent element here forcing a third render state. No destruction groups: it is a static vendor prop, not a breakable. Declared width corrected 1.30 -> 1.08 at model time (2026-09-01). The ten-band proxy comparison read the first build a near-CONSTANT +0.19 of H too wide in every one of bands 0-7 while the DEPTH matched to 0.017 -- a uniform offset across every band is an aspect ratio, not a shape. The proxy wants 0.78 H = 1.09 m, and the plate agrees independently: its silhouette bbox measures w/h 0.896 at the 3/4 view, which a declared 1.30 projects as 1.047 (1.30 cos35 + 0.70 sin35, over 1.40) and 1.08 projects as 0.90. The rebuilt residual is 0.060 width / 0.015 depth against 0.212 / 0.017.
